verses.text: These are the Wise Lessons for Life of Solomon. Solomon was the son of David, king of Israel.
They are given to know wisdom and instruction (correction). They help you perceive (understand) the words of understanding.
They help you receive the instruction (correction) of wisdom. They teach justice, judgment (what is right), and equity (fairness).
They give subtilty (good sense) to the simple (people easily fooled). They give knowledge and discretion (careful thinking) to the young man.
A wise man will hear and will increase in learning. A man of understanding will gain wise counsels (advice).
They help you understand a Wise Lesson for Life and its meaning. They help you understand the words of the wise and their dark sayings (riddles).
The fear of the LORD (deep respect for the LORD) is the beginning of knowledge. But fools despise (look down on) wisdom and instruction (correction).
My son, hear the instruction (correction) of your father. Do not forsake (leave) the law (teaching) of your mother.
This instruction (correction) and law (teaching) will be an ornament of grace (a beautiful crown) on your head. They will be like chains (necklaces) around your neck.
My son, if sinners entice (tempt) you, do not consent (agree).
The sinners may say: Come with us. Let us lay wait (hide and wait) to shed blood. Let us lurk privily (hide secretly) to attack the innocent without cause.
Let us swallow them up alive as the grave does. Let us swallow them whole, like those who go down into the pit.
We will find all kinds of precious things. We will fill our houses with spoil (stolen goods).
Cast in your lot (join) with us. Let us all have one purse (money bag).
My son, do not walk in the way with the sinners. Keep your foot away from their path.
For the sinners' feet run to evil. They make haste (hurry) to shed blood.
Surely the net is spread in vain (for nothing) when any bird can see it.
And the sinners lay wait (hide and wait) for their own blood. They lurk privily (hide secretly) for their own lives.
This is the way of everyone who is greedy of gain (greedy for money). Greed takes away the life of the greedy owners.
Wisdom cries out loud outside. Wisdom lifts up her voice in the streets.
Wisdom cries in the chief place where crowds gather. Wisdom cries at the openings of the gates. In the city Wisdom speaks her words:
How long, you simple (people easily fooled), will you love being simple (easily fooled)? How long will scorners (mockers) delight in their scorning (mocking)? How long will fools hate knowledge?
Turn back at my reproof (correction). Look, I will pour out my spirit to you. I will make my words known to you.
I called, and you refused. I stretched out my hand, and no man regarded (paid attention).
You set at nought (treated as nothing) all my counsel (advice). You would have none of my reproof (correction).
So I also will laugh at your calamity (disaster). I will mock when your fear comes.
Your fear will come as desolation (ruin). Your destruction will come as a whirlwind. Trouble and anguish (deep pain) will come upon you.
Then they will call upon me, but I will not answer. They will seek me early, but they will not find me.
This is because they hated knowledge. They did not choose the fear of the LORD (deep respect for the LORD).
They would have none of my counsel (advice). They despised (looked down on) all my reproof (correction).
So they will eat the fruit of their own way. They will be filled with their own devices (plans).
For the turning away of the simple (people easily fooled) will slay (kill) them. The prosperity (easy life) of fools will destroy them.
But whoever hearkens (listens) to me will dwell (live) safely. The one who listens will be quiet (at rest) from fear of evil.

verses.text: My son, if you will receive my words, and hide (store up) my commandments with you,
So that you incline (turn) your ear to wisdom, and apply your heart to understanding,
Yes, if you cry out for knowledge, and lift up your voice for understanding,
If you seek wisdom as silver, and search for her as for hidden treasures,
Then you will understand the fear of the LORD (deep respect for the LORD). You will find the knowledge of God.
For the LORD gives wisdom. Out of His mouth come knowledge and understanding.
The LORD lays up (stores up) sound wisdom for the righteous (people right with God). He is a buckler (small shield) to those who walk uprightly (honestly).
The LORD keeps the paths of judgment (what is right). He preserves (protects) the way of His saints (holy people).
Then you will understand righteousness (being right with God), judgment (what is right), and equity (fairness). Yes, you will understand every good path.
When wisdom enters into your heart, and knowledge is pleasant to your soul,
Discretion (careful thinking) will preserve (protect) you. Understanding will keep you.
Wisdom will deliver (rescue) you from the way of the evil man. Wisdom will deliver you from the man who speaks froward (twisted) things.
Those evil men leave the paths of uprightness (honest living). They walk in the ways of darkness.
The evil men rejoice to do evil. They delight in the frowardness (twisted ways) of the wicked.
The evil men's ways are crooked. They are froward (twisted) in their paths.
Wisdom will deliver (rescue) you from the strange woman (a woman who is not your wife). She is the stranger who flatters with her words.
The strange woman (a woman who is not your wife) forsakes (leaves) the guide of her youth (the husband of her youth). She forgets the agreement of her God.
For her house inclines (leads down) to death. Her paths lead to the dead.
None who go to her return again. They do not take hold of the paths of life.
So you may walk in the way of good men. You may keep the paths of the righteous (people right with God).
For the upright (honest people) will dwell (live) in the land. The perfect (blameless) will remain in it.
But the wicked will be cut off from the earth. The transgressors (lawbreakers) will be rooted out of it.

verses.text: My son, do not forget my law (teaching). Let your heart keep my commandments.
For my commandments will add to you length of days, long life, and peace.
Do not let mercy and truth forsake (leave) you. Bind them around your neck. Write them on the table (tablet) of your heart.
So you will find favor and good understanding before God and man.
Trust in the LORD with all your heart. Do not lean on your own understanding.
In all your ways acknowledge (recognize) Him. And He will direct your paths.
Do not be wise in your own eyes. Fear the LORD (deeply respect the LORD), and depart (turn away) from evil.
It will be health to your navel (body) and marrow (strength) to your bones.
Honor the LORD with your substance (wealth). Honor Him with the firstfruits (first part) of all your increase (harvest).
So your barns will be filled with plenty. Your presses (winepresses) will burst out with new wine.
My son, do not despise (look down on) the chastening (correction) of the LORD. Do not be weary (tired) of His correction.
For the LORD corrects the one He loves. He is like a father who corrects the son he delights in.
Happy is the man who finds wisdom, and the man who gets understanding.
For the merchandise (trading value) of wisdom is better than the merchandise of silver. Its gain is better than fine gold.
Wisdom is more precious than rubies. All the things you can desire cannot be compared to her.
Length of days is in wisdom's right hand. In her left hand are riches and honor.
Wisdom's ways are ways of pleasantness. All her paths are peace.
Wisdom is a tree of life to those who lay hold on her. Happy is everyone who retains (holds on to) her.
The LORD by wisdom has founded the earth. By understanding He has established (set in place) the heavens.
By His knowledge the depths (deep waters) are broken up. The clouds drop down the dew.
My son, do not let them depart from your eyes. Keep sound wisdom and discretion (careful thinking).
So sound wisdom and discretion (careful thinking) will be life to your soul. They will be grace (beauty) to your neck.
Then you will walk in your way safely. Your foot will not stumble.
When you lie down, you will not be afraid. Yes, you will lie down, and your sleep will be sweet.
Do not be afraid of sudden fear. Do not be afraid of the desolation (ruin) of the wicked when it comes.
For the LORD will be your confidence. The LORD will keep your foot from being taken (caught).
Do not withhold (hold back) good from those to whom it is due. Do not hold it back when your hand has the power to do it.
Do not say to your neighbor: Go, and come again, and tomorrow I will give. Do not say this when you have it with you.
Do not devise (plan) evil against your neighbor. Your neighbor dwells (lives) securely (trusting) by you.
Do not strive (fight) with a man without cause. Do not strive with him if he has done you no harm.
Do not envy the oppressor (one who crushes others). Do not choose any of the oppressor's ways.
For the froward (twisted) person is an abomination (something hated) to the LORD. But His secret is with the righteous (people right with God).
The curse of the LORD is in the house of the wicked. But He blesses the habitation (home) of the just (those who are right with God).
Surely the LORD scorns (mocks) the scorners (mockers). But He gives grace to the lowly (humble).
The wise will inherit glory. But shame will be the promotion of fools.

verses.text: Hear, you children, the instruction (correction) of a father. Pay attention so you will know understanding.
For I give you good doctrine (teaching). Do not forsake (leave) my law (teaching).
For I was my father's son. I was tender (young), and my mother's only beloved (dearly loved) child.
My father taught me too. He said to me: Let your heart retain (hold on to) my words. Keep my commandments, and live.
Get wisdom. Get understanding. Do not forget it. Do not decline (turn away) from the words of my mouth.
Do not forsake (leave) wisdom, and she will preserve (protect) you. Love her, and she will keep you.
Wisdom is the principal (most important) thing. So get wisdom. With all your getting, get understanding.
Exalt (lift up) wisdom, and she will promote you. She will bring you to honor when you embrace (hold close) her.
Wisdom will give your head an ornament of grace (a beautiful crown). She will give you a crown of glory.
Hear, O my son, and receive my sayings. And the years of your life will be many.
I have taught you in the way of wisdom. I have led you in right paths.
When you go, your steps will not be straitened (held back). When you run, you will not stumble.
Take fast hold of instruction (correction). Do not let her go. Keep her, for she is your life.
Do not enter into the path of the wicked. Do not go in the way of evil men.
Avoid the path of the wicked. Do not pass by it. Turn from it, and pass away.
For wicked men do not sleep unless they have done mischief (harm). Their sleep is taken away unless they cause some to fall.
For wicked men eat the bread of wickedness. They drink the wine of violence.
But the path of the just (those who are right with God) is like the shining light. It shines more and more until the perfect day.
The way of the wicked is like darkness. The wicked do not know what makes them stumble.
My son, attend (pay attention) to my words. Incline (turn) your ear to my sayings.
Do not let my words depart from your eyes. Keep them in the middle of your heart.
For my words are life to those who find them. They are health to all their flesh (body).
Keep your heart with all diligence (hard work). For out of your heart are the issues (springs) of life.
Put away from you a froward (twisted) mouth. Put perverse (crooked) lips far from you.
Let your eyes look right on (straight ahead). Let your eyelids look straight before you.
Ponder (weigh carefully) the path of your feet. Let all your ways be established (made firm).
Do not turn to the right hand or to the left. Remove your foot from evil.

verses.text: My son, attend (pay attention) to my wisdom. Bow your ear to my understanding.
Then you may regard (keep) discretion (careful thinking). Your lips may keep knowledge.
For the lips of a strange woman (a woman who is not your wife) drip like a honeycomb. Her mouth is smoother than oil.
But her end is bitter as wormwood (a very bitter plant). It is sharp as a two-edged sword.
Her feet go down to death. Her steps take hold on hell.
Her ways are moveable (always changing), so you cannot know them. This keeps you from pondering (weighing carefully) the path of life.
So hear me now, O you children. Do not depart (turn away) from the words of my mouth.
Remove your way far from the strange woman (a woman who is not your wife). Do not come nigh (near) the door of her house.
Otherwise you will give your honor to others. You will give your years to the cruel.
Otherwise strangers will be filled with your wealth. Your labors (hard work) will be in the house of a stranger.
And you will mourn at the last. You will mourn when your flesh and your body are consumed (worn out).
You will say: How I have hated instruction (correction)! My heart despised (looked down on) reproof (correction)!
I have not obeyed the voice of my teachers. I have not inclined (turned) my ear to those who instructed me!
I was almost in all evil in the middle of the congregation (gathering) and assembly.
Drink waters out of your own cistern (water tank). Drink running waters out of your own well.
Let your fountains (springs) be dispersed (spread) abroad, and rivers of waters in the streets.
Let them be only your own, and not strangers' with you.
Let your fountain (spring) be blessed. Rejoice with the wife of your youth.
Let your wife be like the loving hind (female deer) and pleasant roe (young deer). Let her breasts satisfy you at all times. Always be ravished (carried away) with her love.
And why will you, my son, be ravished (carried away) with a strange woman (a woman who is not your wife)? Why will you embrace the bosom (chest) of a stranger?
For the ways of man are before the eyes of the LORD. The LORD ponders (weighs carefully) all of man's goings.
The wicked man's own iniquities (sins) will take him. He will be holden (held) with the cords (ropes) of his sins.
The wicked man will die without instruction (correction). In the greatness of his folly (foolishness) he will go astray.

verses.text: My son, you may be surety (promise to pay the debt) for your friend. Or you may have stricken your hand (shaken hands to agree) with a stranger.
If so, you are snared (trapped) with the words of your mouth. You are taken (caught) with the words of your mouth.
Do this now, my son, and deliver (rescue) yourself. You have come into the hand (power) of your friend. Go, humble yourself, and make sure (keep begging) your friend.
Do not give sleep to your eyes, or slumber to your eyelids.
Deliver (rescue) yourself as a roe (young deer) from the hand of the hunter. Deliver yourself as a bird from the hand of the fowler (bird catcher).
Go to the ant, you sluggard (lazy person). Consider her ways, and be wise.
The ant has no guide, overseer (boss), or ruler.
Yet the ant provides her meat (food) in the summer. She gathers her food in the harvest.
How long will you sleep, O sluggard (lazy person)? When will you arise out of your sleep?
Yet a little sleep, a little slumber. A little folding of the hands to sleep.
So your poverty will come as one who travels (a wandering robber). Your want (lack) will come as an armed man.
A naughty (worthless) person, a wicked man, walks with a froward (twisted) mouth.
He winks with his eyes. He speaks with his feet. He teaches (points) with his fingers.
Frowardness (twisted ways) is in his heart. He devises (plans) mischief (harm) all the time. He sows discord (plants fighting).
So his calamity (disaster) will come suddenly. Suddenly he will be broken without remedy (cure).
These six things the LORD hates. Yes, seven are an abomination (something hated) to Him:
A proud look, a lying tongue, and hands that shed innocent blood.
A heart that devises (plans) wicked imaginations (ideas). Feet that are swift in running to mischief (harm).
A false witness who speaks lies. And the one who sows discord (plants fighting) among brethren (brothers).
My son, keep your father's commandment. Do not forsake (leave) the law (teaching) of your mother.
Bind them on your heart all the time. Tie them around your neck.
When you go, this teaching will lead you. When you sleep, it will keep you. When you wake, it will talk with you.
For the commandment is a lamp, and the law (teaching) is light. Reproofs (corrections) of instruction (correction) are the way of life.
They keep you from the evil woman. They keep you from the flattery of the tongue of a strange woman (a woman who is not your wife).
Do not lust (wrongly desire) after her beauty in your heart. Do not let her take you with her eyelids.
A whorish woman (a prostitute) brings a man to a piece of bread. And the adulteress (an unfaithful wife) will hunt for the precious life.
Can a man take fire in his bosom (chest) and not burn his clothes?
Can one go on hot coals, and his feet not be burned?
So is the man who goes in to his neighbor's wife. Whoever touches her will not be innocent.
Men do not despise (look down on) a thief if he steals to satisfy his soul (fill himself). The thief steals because he is hungry.
But if the thief is found, he will restore (pay back) sevenfold (seven times). He will give all the substance (wealth) of his house.
But whoever commits adultery (being unfaithful in marriage) with a woman lacks understanding. The one who does it destroys his own soul.
He will get a wound and dishonor. His reproach (shame) will not be wiped away.
For jealousy is the rage of a man. So the husband will not spare in the day of vengeance (paying back).
The husband will not regard (accept) any ransom (the price paid to set people free). He will not rest content, even though you give many gifts.

verses.text: My son, keep my words. Lay up (store up) my commandments with you.
Keep my commandments, and live. Keep my law (teaching) as the apple (pupil) of your eye.
Bind them on your fingers. Write them on the table (tablet) of your heart.
Say to wisdom: You are my sister. Call understanding your kinswoman (close relative).
Then wisdom and understanding may keep you from the strange woman (a woman who is not your wife). They keep you from the stranger who flatters with her words.
For I looked out at the window of my house, through my casement (window lattice).
I beheld (saw) among the simple (people easily fooled). Among the youths I discerned (noticed) a young man void of (empty of) understanding.
The young man was passing through the street near her corner. He went the way to her house.
It was in the twilight, in the evening, in the black and dark night.
And behold (see), a woman met him. She had the attire (clothes) of a harlot (prostitute). She was subtil (crafty) of heart.
She is loud and stubborn. Her feet do not abide (stay) in her house.
Now she is outside, now in the streets. She lies in wait at every corner.
So she caught the young man and kissed him. With an impudent (shameless) face she said to him:
I have peace offerings with me. This day I have paid my vows (promises to God).
So I came out to meet you, diligently (eagerly) to seek your face. And I have found you.
I have decked (covered) my bed with coverings of tapestry (rich cloth). I have covered it with carved works, with fine linen of Egypt.
I have perfumed my bed with myrrh (a bitter spice), aloes (sweet-smelling wood), and cinnamon.
Come, let us take our fill of love until the morning. Let us solace (comfort) ourselves with loves.
For the goodman (husband) is not at home. He has gone on a long journey.
He has taken a bag of money with him. He will come home at the day appointed (set day).
With her much fair speech she caused the young man to yield. With the flattering of her lips she forced him.
He goes after her straightway (right away), as an ox goes to the slaughter. He goes as a fool to the correction of the stocks (wooden chains for the feet).
He goes until a dart (arrow) strikes through his liver. He is like a bird that hastes (hurries) to the snare (trap). He does not know that it is for his life.
So hearken (listen) to me now, O you children. Attend (pay attention) to the words of my mouth.
Do not let your heart decline (turn away) to her ways. Do not go astray in her paths.
For she has cast down many wounded. Yes, many strong men have been slain (killed) by her.
Her house is the way to hell. It goes down to the chambers (rooms) of death.

verses.text: Does not wisdom cry out? Does not understanding put forth her voice?
Wisdom stands on the top of high places. She stands by the way, in the places where the paths meet.
Wisdom cries at the gates, at the entry of the city. She cries at the coming in at the doors:
To you, O men, I call. My voice is to the sons of man (all people).
O you simple (people easily fooled), understand wisdom. And you fools, be of an understanding heart.
Hear, for I will speak of excellent things. The opening of my lips will be right things.
For my mouth will speak truth. Wickedness is an abomination (something hated) to my lips.
All the words of my mouth are in righteousness (being right with God). Nothing froward (twisted) or perverse (crooked) is in them.
My words are all plain to the one who understands. They are right to those who find knowledge.
Receive my instruction (correction), and not silver. Receive knowledge rather than choice gold.
For wisdom is better than rubies. All the things that may be desired cannot be compared to it.
I, Wisdom, dwell (live) with prudence (good sense). I find out knowledge of witty inventions (clever plans).
The fear of the LORD (deep respect for the LORD) is to hate evil. I hate pride, arrogancy (proud talk), the evil way, and the froward (twisted) mouth.
Counsel (advice) is mine, and sound wisdom. I am understanding. I have strength.
By me kings reign (rule). By me princes decree (order) justice.
By me princes rule, and nobles, even all the judges of the earth.
I love those who love me. Those who seek me early will find me.
Riches and honor are with me. Yes, durable (lasting) riches and righteousness (being right with God) are with me.
My fruit is better than gold, yes, than fine gold. My revenue (what I give) is better than choice silver.
I lead in the way of righteousness (being right with God). I lead in the middle of the paths of judgment (what is right).
So I may cause those who love me to inherit substance (wealth). I will fill their treasures.
The LORD possessed (had) me in the beginning of His way. This was before His works of old.
I was set up from everlasting, from the beginning, before the earth ever was.
When there were no depths (deep waters), I was brought forth (born). There were no fountains (springs) abounding (overflowing) with water then.
Before the mountains were settled, before the hills, I was brought forth (born).
The LORD had not yet made the earth or the fields. He had not made the highest part of the dust of the world.
When He prepared the heavens, I was there. I was there when He set a compass (circle) on the face of the depth.
I was there when He established (set in place) the clouds above. I was there when He strengthened the fountains (springs) of the deep.
I was there when He gave to the sea its decree (limit). The waters must not pass His commandment. I was there when He appointed (marked out) the foundations of the earth.
Then I was by Him, as one brought up with Him. I was His delight every day, rejoicing always before Him.
I was rejoicing in the habitable (lived-in) part of His earth. My delights were with the sons of men (people).
So now hearken (listen) to me, O you children. For blessed are those who keep my ways.
Hear instruction (correction), and be wise. Do not refuse it.
Blessed is the man who hears me. He watches every day at my gates. He waits at the posts of my doors.
For whoever finds me finds life. The one who finds me will obtain favor from the LORD.
But the one who sins against me wrongs his own soul. All those who hate me love death.

verses.text: Wisdom has built her house. She has hewn (cut) out her seven pillars.
She has killed her beasts (animals for the meal). She has mingled (mixed) her wine. She has also furnished (set) her table.
She has sent out her maidens (young women servants). She cries on the highest places of the city:
Whoever is simple (easily fooled), let him turn in here. To the one who wants (lacks) understanding, she says:
Come, eat of my bread. Drink of the wine I have mingled (mixed).
Forsake (leave) the foolish, and live. Go in the way of understanding.
The one who reproves (corrects) a scorner (mocker) gets shame for himself. The one who rebukes (scolds) a wicked man gets himself a blot (stain).
Do not reprove (correct) a scorner (mocker), or the scorner (mocker) will hate you. Rebuke (scold) a wise man, and he will love you.
Give instruction (correction) to a wise man, and he will be even wiser. Teach a just (right with God) man, and he will increase in learning.
The fear of the LORD (deep respect for the LORD) is the beginning of wisdom. The knowledge of the holy is understanding.
For by me your days will be multiplied. The years of your life will be increased.
If you are wise, you will be wise for yourself. But if you scorn (mock), you alone will bear it.
A foolish woman is clamorous (loud). She is simple (easily fooled) and knows nothing.
For she sits at the door of her house. She sits on a seat in the high places of the city.
She calls to passengers (people passing by) who go right on their ways:
Whoever is simple (easily fooled), let him turn in here. To the one who wants (lacks) understanding, she says:
Stolen waters are sweet. Bread eaten in secret is pleasant.
But the simple (easily fooled) man does not know that the dead are there. Her guests are in the depths of hell.

verses.text: The Wise Lessons for Life of Solomon. A wise son makes a glad father. But a foolish son is the heaviness (sorrow) of his mother.
Treasures of wickedness profit nothing. But righteousness (being right with God) delivers (rescues) from death.
The LORD will not suffer (allow) the soul of the righteous (people right with God) to famish (starve). But He casts away the substance (wealth) of the wicked.
The one who deals with a slack (lazy) hand becomes poor. But the hand of the diligent (hard worker) makes rich.
He who gathers in summer is a wise son. But he who sleeps in harvest is a son who causes shame.
Blessings are on the head of the just (those who are right with God). But violence covers the mouth of the wicked.
The memory of the just (those who are right with God) is blessed. But the name of the wicked will rot.
The wise in heart will receive commandments. But a prating (foolishly talking) fool will fall.
The one who walks uprightly (honestly) walks surely (safely). But the one who perverts (twists) his ways will be known.
The one who winks with the eye causes sorrow. But a prating (foolishly talking) fool will fall.
The mouth of a righteous (right with God) man is a well of life. But violence covers the mouth of the wicked.
Hatred stirs up strifes (fights). But love covers all sins.
Wisdom is found in the lips of the one who has understanding. But a rod is for the back of the one void of (empty of) understanding.
Wise men lay up (store up) knowledge. But the mouth of the foolish is near destruction.
The rich man's wealth is his strong city. The destruction of the poor is their poverty.
The labor (hard work) of the righteous (people right with God) leads to life. The fruit of the wicked leads to sin.
The one who keeps instruction (correction) is in the way of life. But the one who refuses reproof (correction) errs (goes wrong).
The one who hides hatred with lying lips is a fool. The one who utters (speaks) a slander (a lie that hurts someone) is a fool.
In the multitude of words, sin is not lacking. But the one who refrains (holds back) his lips is wise.
The tongue of the just (those who are right with God) is like choice silver. The heart of the wicked is worth little.
The lips of the righteous (people right with God) feed many. But fools die for want (lack) of wisdom.
The blessing of the LORD makes rich. And He adds no sorrow with it.
It is like sport (a game) to a fool to do mischief (harm). But a man of understanding has wisdom.
The fear of the wicked will come upon the wicked man. But the desire of the righteous (people right with God) will be granted.
As the whirlwind passes, so the wicked is no more. But the righteous (people right with God) are an everlasting foundation.
The sluggard (lazy person) is like vinegar to the teeth and smoke to the eyes. He is like that to those who send him.
The fear of the LORD (deep respect for the LORD) prolongs (lengthens) days. But the years of the wicked will be shortened.
The hope of the righteous (people right with God) will be gladness. But the expectation of the wicked will perish (be destroyed).
The way of the LORD is strength to the upright (honest people). But destruction will be to the workers of iniquity (sin).
The righteous (people right with God) will never be removed. But the wicked will not inhabit (live in) the earth.
The mouth of the just (those who are right with God) brings forth (produces) wisdom. But the froward (twisted) tongue will be cut out.
The lips of the righteous (people right with God) know what is acceptable (pleasing). But the mouth of the wicked speaks frowardness (twisted ways).

verses.text: A false balance (dishonest scale) is an abomination (something hated) to the LORD. But a just (honest) weight is His delight.
When pride comes, then shame comes. But with the lowly (humble) is wisdom.
The integrity (honesty) of the upright (honest people) will guide them. But the perverseness (crookedness) of transgressors (lawbreakers) will destroy them.
Riches do not profit in the day of wrath (God's anger). But righteousness (being right with God) delivers (rescues) from death.
The righteousness (being right with God) of the perfect (blameless) will direct his way. But the wicked will fall by his own wickedness.
The righteousness (being right with God) of the upright (honest people) will deliver (rescue) them. But transgressors (lawbreakers) will be taken in their own naughtiness (evil desire).
When a wicked man dies, his expectation will perish (be destroyed). And the hope of unjust men perishes (is destroyed).
The righteous (right with God) man is delivered (rescued) out of trouble. And the wicked man comes in his stead (place).
A hypocrite (pretender) with his mouth destroys his neighbor. But through knowledge the just (those who are right with God) will be delivered (rescued).
When it goes well with the righteous (people right with God), the city rejoices. When the wicked perish (are destroyed), there is shouting.
By the blessing of the upright (honest people) the city is exalted (lifted up). But it is overthrown by the mouth of the wicked.
The one who is void of (empty of) wisdom despises (looks down on) his neighbor. But a man of understanding holds his peace (stays quiet).
A talebearer (gossip) reveals secrets. But the one who has a faithful spirit conceals (hides) the matter.
Where no counsel (advice) is, the people fall. But in the multitude of counsellors (advisers) there is safety.
The one who is surety (promise to pay the debt) for a stranger will smart (suffer) for it. The one who hates suretiship (promising to pay another's debt) is sure (safe).
A gracious woman retains (keeps) honor. And strong men retain (keep) riches.
The merciful man does good to his own soul. But the one who is cruel troubles his own flesh (body).
The wicked man works a deceitful (lying) work. But the one who sows (plants) righteousness (being right with God) will have a sure reward.
Righteousness (being right with God) leads to life. So the one who pursues (chases) evil pursues it to his own death.
Those who have a froward (twisted) heart are an abomination (something hated) to the LORD. But those who are upright (honest) in their way are His delight.
Though hand join in hand (they join together), the wicked will not be unpunished. But the seed (children) of the righteous (people right with God) will be delivered (rescued).
A jewel of gold in a swine's (pig's) snout. That is what a fair (beautiful) woman without discretion (careful thinking) is like.
The desire of the righteous (people right with God) is only good. But the expectation of the wicked is wrath (God's anger).
There is one who scatters, and yet increases. There is one who withholds (holds back) more than is meet (right). But it leads to poverty.
The liberal (generous) soul will be made fat (rich). The one who waters will be watered also himself.
The people will curse the one who withholds (holds back) corn (grain). But blessing will be on the head of the one who sells it.
The one who diligently (eagerly) seeks good procures (gets) favor. But the one who seeks mischief (harm), it will come to him.
The one who trusts in his riches will fall. But the righteous (people right with God) will flourish like a branch.
The one who troubles his own house will inherit the wind. And the fool will be servant to the wise of heart.
The fruit of the righteous (people right with God) is a tree of life. And the one who wins souls is wise.
Behold (see), the righteous (people right with God) will be recompensed (repaid) in the earth. Much more the wicked and the sinner.

verses.text: Whoever loves instruction (correction) loves knowledge. But the one who hates reproof (correction) is brutish (stupid like an animal).
A good man obtains (gets) favor from the LORD. But a man of wicked devices (plans) He will condemn (judge guilty).
A man will not be established (made firm) by wickedness. But the root of the righteous (people right with God) will not be moved.
A virtuous (good and strong) woman is a crown to her husband. But she who makes him ashamed is like rottenness in his bones.
The thoughts of the righteous (people right with God) are right. But the counsels (advice) of the wicked are deceit (lying).
The words of the wicked are to lie in wait for blood. But the mouth of the upright (honest people) will deliver (rescue) them.
The wicked are overthrown, and are no more. But the house of the righteous (people right with God) will stand.
A man will be commended (praised) according to his wisdom. But the one who has a perverse (crooked) heart will be despised (looked down on).
The one who is despised (looked down on) and has a servant is better off. He is better than the one who honors himself and lacks bread.
A righteous (right with God) man regards (cares for) the life of his beast (animal). But the tender mercies of the wicked are cruel.
The one who tills (works) his land will be satisfied with bread. But the one who follows vain (worthless) persons is void of (empty of) understanding.
The wicked desires the net of evil men. But the root of the righteous (people right with God) yields (gives) fruit.
The wicked man is snared (trapped) by the transgression (sin) of his lips. But the just (those who are right with God) will come out of trouble.
A man will be satisfied with good by the fruit of his mouth. The recompense (repayment) of a man's hands will be rendered (given) to him.
The way of a fool is right in his own eyes. But the one who hearkens (listens) to counsel (advice) is wise.
A fool's wrath (anger) is presently (right away) known. But a prudent (sensible) man covers shame.
The one who speaks truth shows forth righteousness (being right with God). But a false witness shows deceit (lying).
There is one who speaks like the piercings of a sword. But the tongue of the wise is health.
The lip of truth will be established (made firm) forever. But a lying tongue is only for a moment.
Deceit (lying) is in the heart of those who imagine (plan) evil. But to the counsellors (advisers) of peace is joy.
No evil will happen to the just (those who are right with God). But the wicked will be filled with mischief (harm).
Lying lips are an abomination (something hated) to the LORD. But those who deal truly are His delight.
A prudent (sensible) man conceals (hides) knowledge. But the heart of fools proclaims (announces) foolishness.
The hand of the diligent (hard worker) will bear rule (rule). But the slothful (lazy) will be under tribute (forced work).
Heaviness (sorrow) in the heart of man makes it stoop (bow down). But a good word makes it glad.
The righteous (right with God) man is more excellent than his neighbor. But the way of the wicked seduces (leads astray) them.
The slothful (lazy) man does not roast what he took in hunting. But the substance (wealth) of a diligent (hard working) man is precious.
In the way of righteousness (being right with God) is life. In its pathway there is no death.

verses.text: A wise son hears his father's instruction (correction). But a scorner (mocker) does not hear rebuke (scolding).
A man will eat good by the fruit of his mouth. But the soul of the transgressors (lawbreakers) will eat violence.
The one who keeps (guards) his mouth keeps his life. But the one who opens wide his lips will have destruction.
The soul of the sluggard (lazy person) desires, and has nothing. But the soul of the diligent (hard worker) will be made fat (rich).
A righteous (right with God) man hates lying. But a wicked man is loathsome (disgusting), and comes to shame.
Righteousness (being right with God) keeps the one who is upright (honest) in the way. But wickedness overthrows the sinner.
There is one who makes himself rich, yet has nothing. There is one who makes himself poor, yet has great riches.
The ransom (the price paid to set people free) of a man's life is his riches. But the poor man does not hear rebuke (scolding).
The light of the righteous (people right with God) rejoices. But the lamp of the wicked will be put out.
Only by pride comes contention (fighting). But with the well advised is wisdom.
Wealth gotten by vanity (emptiness) will be diminished (made smaller). But the one who gathers by labor (hard work) will increase.
Hope deferred (put off) makes the heart sick. But when the desire comes, it is a tree of life.
Whoever despises (looks down on) the word will be destroyed. But the one who fears (deeply respects) the commandment will be rewarded.
The law (teaching) of the wise is a fountain (spring) of life. It helps you depart (turn away) from the snares (traps) of death.
Good understanding gives favor. But the way of transgressors (lawbreakers) is hard.
Every prudent (sensible) man deals with knowledge. But a fool lays open his folly (foolishness).
A wicked messenger falls into mischief (harm). But a faithful ambassador (messenger) is health.
Poverty and shame will be to the one who refuses instruction (correction). But the one who regards (pays attention to) reproof (correction) will be honored.
The desire accomplished is sweet to the soul. But it is an abomination (something hated) to fools to depart (turn away) from evil.
The one who walks with wise men will be wise. But a companion of fools will be destroyed.
Evil pursues (chases) sinners. But to the righteous (people right with God) good will be repaid.
A good man leaves an inheritance to his children's children. The wealth of the sinner is laid up (stored up) for the just (those who are right with God).
Much food is in the tillage (farm field) of the poor. But some is destroyed for want (lack) of judgment (what is right).
The one who spares his rod hates his son. But the one who loves his son chastens (corrects) him betimes (early).
The righteous (right with God) man eats to the satisfying of his soul. But the belly (stomach) of the wicked will want (lack).

verses.text: Every wise woman builds up her house, but a foolish woman tears it down with her own hands.
Whoever walks with integrity respects the LORD, but a devious person despises the LORD.
A fool's talk brings a rod of pride, but the lips of the wise protect the wise.
Where there are no oxen, the feeding trough is empty, but a strong ox brings a large harvest.
A truthful witness does not lie, but a false witness pours out lies.
A mocker looks for wisdom and never finds it, but knowledge comes easily to someone with understanding.
Stay away from a fool, because you will not find knowledge on a fool's lips.
The wisdom of a sensible person is to understand a sensible person's own way, but the foolishness of fools is deception.
Fools laugh at making up for their sins, but goodwill is found among the honest.
The heart knows its own bitterness, and no stranger can share its joy.
The house of the wicked will be destroyed, but the tent of honest people will flourish.
There is a way that seems right to a person, but in the end it leads to death.
Even in laughter the heart may ache, and joy may end in sorrow.
A faithless person will be paid back for their own ways, and a good person will be rewarded for theirs.
The simple believe anything, but a sensible person watches their step.
A wise person is careful and turns away from evil, but a fool is reckless and overconfident.
A quick-tempered person acts foolishly, and a schemer is hated.
The simple inherit foolishness, but the sensible are crowned with knowledge.
Evil people will bow before the good, and the wicked at the gates of the righteous.
Poor people are disliked even by their own neighbors, but rich people have many friends.
Whoever looks down on a neighbor sins, but blessed is whoever is kind to the poor.
Don't those who plan evil go astray? But those who plan good find love and faithfulness.
All hard work brings profit, but mere talk leads only to poverty.
The wealth of the wise is their crown, but the foolishness of fools stays foolish.
A truthful witness saves lives, but a deceitful witness pours out lies.
Respecting the LORD is a strong fortress that gives a person's children a place of safety.
Respecting the LORD is a fountain of life, turning a person away from the snares of death.
A large population is a king's glory, but without people a ruler is ruined.
Whoever is patient has great understanding, but whoever is quick-tempered displays foolishness.
A calm heart gives life to the body, but jealousy rots the bones.
Whoever oppresses the poor insults God, the Maker of all, but whoever is kind to the needy honors God.
The wicked are brought down by their own wrongdoing, but the righteous have a refuge even in death.
Wisdom rests in the heart of someone with understanding, and even among fools wisdom becomes known.
Righteousness lifts up a nation, but sin is a disgrace to any people.
A king favors a wise servant, but a king's anger falls on one who brings shame.

14.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked against the Hebrew text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy. verses.text: A gentle answer turns away anger, but harsh words stir up wrath.
The tongue of the wise uses knowledge well, but the mouth of fools pours out foolishness.
The eyes of the LORD are everywhere, watching over both the evil and the good.
Healing words are a tree of life, but deceitful words crush the spirit.
A fool despises a father's instruction, but whoever accepts correction is sensible.
In the house of the righteous there is great treasure, but the earnings of the wicked bring trouble.
The lips of the wise spread knowledge, but the hearts of fools are not so honest.
The LORD hates the sacrifice of the wicked, but the LORD delights in the prayer of honest people.
The LORD hates the way of the wicked, but the LORD loves whoever pursues righteousness.
Strict discipline awaits whoever leaves the right path; whoever hates correction will die.
Hell and destruction lie open before the LORD; how much more, then, the hearts of people!
A mocker does not like being corrected, and will not seek advice from the wise.
A happy heart makes a cheerful face, but heartache crushes the spirit.
The heart of someone with understanding seeks knowledge, but the mouth of fools feeds on foolishness.
All the days of the oppressed are hard, but a cheerful heart has a continual feast.
Better a little with respect for the LORD than great treasure with turmoil.
Better a meal of vegetables where there is love than a feast of meat with hatred.
A hot-tempered person stirs up conflict, but whoever is patient calms a dispute.
The way of the lazy person is blocked with thorns, but the path of honest people is a highway.
A wise child brings joy to a father, but a foolish person despises their mother.
Foolishness brings joy to someone with no sense, but a person with understanding walks a straight path.
Plans fail without good advice, but they succeed with many advisers.
A person finds joy in giving a good answer, and how good is a word spoken at just the right time!
For a wise person, the path of life leads upward, away from hell below.
The LORD tears down the house of the proud, but the LORD protects the widow's boundaries.
The LORD hates the thoughts of the wicked, but pure words are pleasing to the LORD.
Greed brings trouble on a person's own family, but whoever hates bribes will live.
The heart of the righteous thinks carefully before answering, but the mouth of the wicked pours out evil.
The LORD is far from the wicked, but the LORD hears the prayer of the righteous.
A cheerful look brings joy to the heart, and good news gives strength to the body.
Whoever listens to life-giving correction will be at home among the wise.
Whoever ignores discipline despises themselves, but whoever accepts correction gains understanding.
Respecting the LORD teaches wisdom, and humility comes before honor.

15.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked against the Hebrew text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy. V11 and v24's 'hell' rendered 'the grave' / 'the grave below' (Hebrew sheol), consistent with earlier chapters.

verses.text: A person can plan that person's own thoughts, but the answer on the tongue comes from the LORD.
All a person's ways seem right in that person's own eyes, but the LORD weighs the motives.
Commit your work to the LORD, and your plans will succeed.
The LORD has made everything for its purpose, even the wicked for the day of trouble.
The LORD hates everyone who is proud in heart; be sure of this: a proud person will not go unpunished.
Through love and faithfulness sin is atoned for; through respecting the LORD a person turns away from evil.
When a person's ways please the LORD, the LORD makes even that person's enemies live at peace with that person.
Better a little with righteousness than great income with injustice.
A person's heart plans that person's path, but the LORD directs that person's steps.
The king speaks with divine authority; the king's mouth must not betray justice.
Honest scales and balances belong to the LORD; all the weights in the bag are the LORD's work.
Kings hate wrongdoing, because a throne is made secure through righteousness.
Honest lips please kings; kings value someone who speaks the truth.
A king's anger is a messenger of death, but a wise person will calm that anger.
When a king's face lights up, there is life; the king's favor is like a rain cloud in spring.
How much better to get wisdom than gold! To gain understanding is better than silver!
The highway of honest people avoids evil; whoever watches that person's own step protects that person's own life.
Pride goes before destruction, and a proud spirit before a fall.
Better to be humble with the poor than to share plunder with the proud.
Whoever handles a matter wisely finds success, and blessed is whoever trusts in the LORD.
The wise in heart are called understanding, and pleasant words make instruction persuasive.
Understanding is a fountain of life to those who have it, but instruction is wasted on fools.
The heart of a wise person makes that person's words wise, and that person's lips become more persuasive.
Pleasant words are like a honeycomb, sweet to the soul and healing to the bones.
There is a way that seems right to a person, but in the end it leads to death.
A worker's appetite works for the worker; the worker's hunger drives the worker on.
A worthless person digs up evil, and that person's words are like a scorching fire.
A dishonest person spreads conflict, and a gossip separates close friends.
A violent person lures a neighbor and leads the neighbor down a path that is not good.
Whoever squints their eyes is plotting dishonesty; whoever bites their lips is bent on evil.
Gray hair is a crown of glory, found in the way of righteousness.
Better to be patient than powerful, and better to control your temper than to capture a city.
The lot may be cast into the lap, but the LORD alone decides the outcome.

16.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked against the Hebrew text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy. verses.text: Better a dry piece of bread eaten in peace than a house full of feasting with conflict.
A wise servant will rule over a shameful son, and that wise servant will share the inheritance among the brothers.
The furnace tests silver, and the fire tests gold, but the LORD tests hearts.
An evildoer listens to wicked lips; a liar pays attention to a destructive tongue.
Whoever mocks the poor insults God, the Maker of all; whoever is glad at another's trouble will not go unpunished.
Grandchildren are the crown of the elderly, and parents are the pride of their own children.
Fine words do not fit a fool; even less do lying lips fit a ruler.
A gift is like a precious stone to the person who gives it; that gift succeeds wherever it goes.
Whoever covers over an offense seeks love, but whoever repeats a matter separates close friends.
A rebuke cuts deeper into a wise person than a hundred lashes cut into a fool.
An evil person seeks only rebellion, so a cruel messenger will be sent against that evil person.
Better to meet a bear robbed of her cubs than to meet a fool in that fool's foolishness.
If anyone repays evil for good, evil will never leave that person's house.
Starting a conflict is like breaking open a dam, so stop the argument before the flood begins.
Whoever declares the guilty innocent, and whoever condemns the innocent — both are disgusting to the LORD.
Why should a fool pay money to gain wisdom, when that fool has no desire to learn it?
A friend loves at all times, and a family member is born for times of trouble.
A person with no sense shakes hands to guarantee a loan, and becomes responsible for a neighbor's debt.
Whoever loves conflict loves sin; whoever builds a high gate invites disaster.
Whoever has a dishonest heart finds no good; whoever has a lying tongue falls into trouble.
The parent of a fool will grieve; the father of a fool has no joy.
A cheerful heart is good medicine, but a crushed spirit is like draining a person's strength.
A wicked person takes a secret bribe to twist the course of justice.
Wisdom is right in front of someone with understanding, but a fool's eyes wander to the ends of the earth.
A foolish son brings grief to that son's father, and bitterness to the mother who bore that son.
It is not good to punish the innocent or to whip officials for their honesty.
Whoever has knowledge holds back words, and a person of understanding stays calm.
Even a fool who stays quiet seems wise; closed lips seem wise and understanding.

17.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Hebrew text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy, with every pronoun's referent named explicitly (Deaf-first clarity standard) and each verse capitalized. verses.text: Whoever separates himself from others pursues selfish desires, and rebels against all sound judgment.
A fool takes no pleasure in understanding, but only in expressing a fool's own opinions.
When wickedness comes, contempt comes too, and with shame comes scorn.
The words of a person's mouth are like deep waters, and the fountain of wisdom is like a flowing brook.
It is not good to favor the guilty and deprive the innocent of justice.
A fool's lips lead to arguments, and a fool's mouth invites a beating.
A fool's mouth is a fool's ruin, and a fool's lips are a trap for a fool's own life.
The words of a gossip are like delicious food; they go down to the innermost parts of the body.
Whoever is lazy in work is a close relative to someone who destroys.
The name of the LORD is a strong tower; the righteous run into it and are safe.
The wealth of the rich is the rich person's strong city; the rich person imagines it as a high wall.
Before destruction a person's heart is proud, but humility comes before honor.
Whoever answers before listening — that is foolish and shameful.
A person's spirit can carry that person through sickness, but who can bear a broken spirit?
A sensible mind gains knowledge, and the ears of the wise seek knowledge.
A gift opens doors for the giver and brings the giver before important people.
The first person to speak in a dispute seems right, until someone else comes and cross-examines that first person.
Casting the lot settles arguments and keeps strong opponents apart.
An offended family member is harder to win back than a fortified city, and disputes between family members are like the barred gates of a fortress.
A person's stomach is filled by the fruit of that person's mouth; that person is satisfied by the harvest of that person's own lips.
Death and life are in the power of the tongue, and whoever loves talking will eat the fruit that talking produces.
Whoever finds a wife finds a good thing, and receives favor from the LORD.
The poor person pleads, but the rich person answers harshly.
Some friendships lead only to ruin, but a friend can stick closer than a brother.

18.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Hebrew text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy, with every pronoun's referent named explicitly (Deaf-first clarity standard) and each verse capitalized.
