verses.text: The king's heart is like a stream of water in the LORD's hand; the LORD directs it wherever the LORD wants.
Every way of a person seems right in that person's own eyes, but the LORD examines the heart.
Doing what is just and right pleases the LORD more than sacrifice.
Proud eyes and an arrogant heart — the lamp that guides the wicked — are sin.
The plans of a hard worker lead only to profit, but everyone who is hasty ends only in poverty.
Wealth gained by a lying tongue is like a fleeting mist, a deadly trap for those who seek it.
The violence of the wicked will destroy the wicked, because the wicked refuse to do what is right.
The way of the guilty is crooked, but the conduct of the innocent is upright.
Better to live on a corner of the roof than to share a house with a quarrelsome wife.
The wicked person craves evil; that wicked person's neighbor finds no mercy in that wicked person's eyes.
When a mocker is punished, the simple become wise; when the wise are instructed, the wise gain knowledge.
A righteous person carefully watches the house of the wicked, but God brings the wicked to ruin for their wickedness.
Whoever shuts their ears to the cry of the poor will also cry out and not be answered.
A secret gift calms anger, and a hidden bribe calms great wrath.
When justice is done, it brings joy to the righteous, but terror to those who do wrong.
Whoever wanders from the way of understanding will end up in the company of the dead.
Whoever loves pleasure will become poor; whoever loves wine and luxury will never be rich.
The wicked become a ransom for the righteous, and the treacherous for the honest.
Better to live in a desert than with a quarrelsome, ill-tempered wife.
The wise have precious treasure and olive oil in their homes, but a foolish person swallows up everything that foolish person has.
Whoever pursues righteousness and mercy finds life, righteousness, and honor.
A wise person can scale a city defended by warriors and bring down the fortress the warriors trusted.
Whoever guards their mouth and tongue keeps themselves out of trouble.
A proud and arrogant person — Mocker is that person's name — acts with overflowing pride.
The craving of a lazy person will kill that lazy person, because that lazy person's hands refuse to work.
All day long the greedy person craves more, but the righteous person gives without holding back.
The sacrifice of the wicked is disgusting to the LORD — even more so when brought with an evil motive.
A false witness will perish, but a truthful witness will speak on and endure.
A wicked person puts on a bold face, but an honest person thinks carefully about that honest person's own ways.
No wisdom, no understanding, no plan can succeed against the LORD.
The horse is prepared for the day of battle, but victory belongs to the LORD.

21.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Hebrew text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy, with every pronoun's referent named explicitly (Deaf-first clarity standard) and each verse capitalized. V4's debated Hebrew word (KJV: 'plowing') rendered as 'lamp,' the well-supported modern reading.

verses.text: A good name is worth more than great riches, and being well thought of is worth more than silver and gold.
Rich and poor have this in common: the LORD made them both.
A sensible person sees danger and hides, but the simple keep going and suffer for it.
Humility and respecting the LORD bring riches, honor, and life.
Thorns and snares are on the path of a dishonest person, but whoever guards their own life stays far from them.
Train up a child in the way that child should go, and when that child is old, that child will not turn from it.
The rich rule over the poor, and the borrower is a slave to the lender.
Whoever plants injustice will harvest disaster, and the weapon of that person's fury will fail.
A generous person will be blessed, because that generous person shares food with the poor.
Drive out a mocker, and conflict goes with the mocker; arguing and insults will stop.
Whoever loves a pure heart and speaks with grace will have the king as a friend.
The eyes of the LORD watch over knowledge, but the LORD overturns the words of the unfaithful.
A lazy person says: There is a lion outside! I will be killed in the streets!
The mouth of a woman who is unfaithful is a deep pit; whoever is under the LORD's anger will fall into it.
Foolishness is tied up in a child's heart, but the rod of discipline will drive it far from that child.
Whoever oppresses the poor to grow rich, and whoever gives gifts to the rich, will both come to poverty.
Listen closely, and hear the words of the wise; apply your heart to my knowledge,
because it is pleasant to keep these words within you, ready on your lips.
So that your trust may be in the LORD, I am teaching you today, yes, you.
Have I not written for you thirty sayings, full of good advice and knowledge,
so that you may know the truth of these reliable words, and take back a true answer to the one who sent you?
Do not rob the poor because they are poor, and do not crush the needy in court,
because the LORD will take up their case, and will take the life of those who take advantage of them.
Do not make friends with an angry person, and do not associate with anyone who has a hot temper,
or you may learn that hot-tempered person's ways and set a trap for your own soul.
Do not be one who shakes hands in agreement or puts up security for debts.
If you have nothing to pay with, why should your bed be taken from under you?
Do not move an ancient boundary stone that your ancestors set up.
Do you see someone skilled in their work? That skilled person will serve before kings, not before unknown people.

22.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Hebrew text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy, with every pronoun's referent named explicitly (Deaf-first clarity standard) and each verse capitalized. V20 corrected from KJV's 'excellent things' to 'thirty sayings,' the well-supported modern reading -- this section of Proverbs (22:17-24:22) is understood as a collection of exactly 30 wisdom sayings, paralleling a similar ancient Egyptian wisdom text.

verses.text: When you sit down to eat with a ruler, pay close attention to what is in front of you,
And put a knife to your own throat if you are a person who has a big appetite.
Do not crave that ruler's delicacies, because that food is deceptive.
Do not wear yourself out to get rich; be wise enough to stop.
Will you set your eyes on riches, when they are gone in an instant? Riches sprout wings and fly away like an eagle into the sky!
Do not eat the food of a stingy person, and do not crave that stingy person's delicacies,
Because that stingy person is always thinking about the cost of food. Eat and drink, that stingy person says to you, but that stingy person's heart is not with you.
You will vomit up the little you have eaten, and waste your pleasant words.
Do not speak to a fool, because that fool will scorn the wisdom of your words.
Do not move an ancient boundary stone, and do not encroach on the fields of orphans,
Because the Defender of orphans is strong; that strong Defender will take up the court case of orphans against you.
Apply your heart to instruction, and your ears to words of knowledge.
Do not withhold discipline from a child; if you punish that child with the rod, that child will not die.
Punish that child with the rod, and deliver that child's soul from hell.
My son, if your heart is wise, then my own heart will rejoice.
Yes, my inmost being will rejoice when your lips speak what is right.
Do not let your heart envy sinners, but always continue to respect the LORD.
Because there is surely a future ahead, and your hope will not be cut off.
Listen, my son, and be wise; keep your heart on the right path.
Do not join those who drink too much wine or those who feast on meat without restraint,
Because drunkards and gluttons become poor, and drowsiness dresses a person in rags.
Listen to your father who gave you life, and do not look down on your mother when she is old.
Buy the truth and do not sell it — buy wisdom, instruction, and understanding too.
The father of a righteous child will rejoice greatly; whoever has a wise child will delight in that child.
Let your father and your mother be glad; let the mother who bore you rejoice.
My son, give me your heart, and let your eyes watch my ways carefully.
Because a prostitute is a deep pit, and a woman who is unfaithful is a narrow well.
She lies in wait like a robber, and she increases the number of unfaithful men.
Who has trouble? Who has sorrow? Who has fights? Who has complaints? Who has wounds for no reason? Who has bloodshot eyes?
Those who spend too much time drinking wine, those who go looking for mixed wine.
Do not look at the wine when it is red, when that wine sparkles in the cup, when that wine goes down smoothly.
In the end, that wine bites like a poisonous snake and stings like a viper.
Your eyes will see strange things, and your mind will imagine confused thoughts.
You will be like someone lying down in the middle of the sea, or someone lying on top of a ship's mast.
People hit me, you will say, but I did not feel it; people beat me, but I did not know it. When will I wake up? I will look for another drink.

23.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Hebrew text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy, with every pronoun's referent named explicitly (Deaf-first clarity standard) and each verse capitalized. V14's 'hell' corrected to 'the grave' (Hebrew sheol), consistent with the rest of the book. V11 identifies God as 'the Defender' of orphans explicitly; v35 specifies 'People' rather than 'they' for the drunken tavern fight scene.

verses.text: Do not envy wicked people, and do not desire to be with evil people,
Because the hearts of evil people plan destruction, and the lips of evil people talk about trouble.
A house is built by wisdom, and it becomes strong through understanding.
Through knowledge its rooms are filled with rare and beautiful treasures.
A wise person is strong, and someone with knowledge grows stronger and stronger.
Because with wise guidance you can wage war, and victory comes with many advisers.
Wisdom is too high for a fool; a fool has nothing to say in the assembly at the gate.
Whoever plans evil will be called a schemer.
The schemes of a fool are sin, and people despise a mocker.
If you give up when trouble comes, how small your strength really is!
Rescue those being dragged toward death, and save people who are staggering toward execution.

If you say: We did not know about this — does the LORD, who weighs hearts, not see it? Does the One who watches over your life not know it? Will the LORD not repay each person for what that person has done?
My son, eat honey, because it is good; the honeycomb is sweet to your taste.
Know that wisdom is sweet to your soul in the exact same way; if you find it, there is a future for you, and your hope will not be cut off.
Do not lie in ambush like a wicked person against the home of the righteous; do not destroy the righteous person's resting place,
Because a righteous person falls seven times and gets back up again, but wicked people stumble into ruin when trouble comes.
Do not rejoice when your enemy falls, and do not let your heart be glad when your enemy stumbles,
Or the LORD will see your pride, and the LORD will be displeased and turn His anger away from your enemy.
Do not fret because of evildoers, and do not envy the wicked,
Because the evil person has no future; the lamp of the wicked will be put out.
My son, respect the LORD and the king, and do not join with rebels,
Because destruction will strike rebels suddenly, and who knows what ruin the LORD and the king can bring?
These also are sayings of the wise: It is not good to show favoritism in judging.
Whoever tells the guilty: You are innocent — people will curse that person, and nations will despise that person.
But it will go well for those who convict the guilty, and rich blessing will come on them.
Giving an honest answer is as refreshing as a kiss on the lips.
Finish your outdoor work, and get your fields ready; after that, build your house.
Do not testify against your neighbor without a reason, and do not deceive with your lips.
Do not say: I will do to that person what that person did to me; I will pay that person back for what that person has done.
I walked past the field of a lazy person, by the vineyard of someone with no sense,
And that field was completely overgrown with thorns, weeds covered the ground, and the stone wall was broken down.
I looked and thought carefully about what I had seen, and I learned this lesson:
A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to rest,
And poverty will come on you like a robber, and need like an armed soldier.

24.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Hebrew text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy, with every pronoun's referent named explicitly (Deaf-first clarity standard) and each verse capitalized. Vocabulary refined throughout for clearer, more direct visual language (v11, v14, v26, v30-31), and remaining vague pronouns (v1-2, v16, v18, v22) replaced with explicit nouns.

verses.text: These are more sayings of Solomon, which the officials of King Hezekiah of Judah copied down.
It is the glory of God to hide a matter, but the glory of kings is to search it out.
The heavens are high, and the earth is deep, and the hearts of kings cannot be searched out.
Remove the impurities from silver, and a craftsman can shape it into a vessel.
Remove wicked advisers from the king's presence, and the king's throne will be made secure through righteousness.
Do not push yourself forward in the king's presence, and do not stand in the place of important people,
Because it is better for the king to say: Come up here! It is worse for him to demote you in front of a noble person.
Do not rush into a lawsuit, because what will you do in the end if your neighbor puts you to shame?
Argue your case with your neighbor directly, and do not reveal another person's secret,
Or whoever hears it may shame you, and your bad reputation will never go away.
A word spoken at the right time is like golden apples arranged in silver settings.
Like a gold earring or a fine gold ornament is a wise correction to a listening ear.
Like the coolness of snow at harvest time, a trustworthy messenger refreshes the spirit of the leader who sent that messenger.
Whoever boasts about a gift never given is like clouds and wind that bring no rain.
Through patience a ruler can be persuaded, and gentle speech can break down strong resistance.
If you find honey, eat only what you need, or you will eat too much and vomit.
Rarely set foot in your neighbor's house, or your neighbor will get tired of you and come to hate you.
Whoever gives false testimony against a neighbor is like a club, a sword, or a sharp arrow.
Trusting an unfaithful person in a time of trouble is like a broken tooth or a foot that slips.
Like taking away a coat on a freezing day, or pouring vinegar on baking soda, so is singing happy songs to a sad heart.
If your enemy is hungry, give your enemy bread to eat, and if your enemy is thirsty, give your enemy water to drink,
Because you will heap burning coals on your enemy's head, and the LORD will reward you.
Just as the north wind brings rain, a gossiping tongue brings angry looks.
Better to live on a corner of the roof than to share a house with a quarrelsome wife.
Like cold water to a weary soul is good news from a distant land.
Like a muddied spring or a polluted well is a righteous person who gives way before the wicked.
It is not good to eat too much honey, and it is not good to seek honor for yourself.
Whoever cannot control their own temper is like a city with its protective walls broken down.

25.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Hebrew text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy, with every pronoun's referent named explicitly (Deaf-first clarity standard) and each verse capitalized. V15 clarified so 'break a bone' isn't misread as literal violence (the Hebrew idiom is about persistence overcoming stubbornness). V20 kept accurate to the Hebrew's chemical-reaction image (vinegar on soda/natron) rather than shifting to a wound metaphor. V21-22's 'burning coals' left as the text states, without adding an interpretive gloss like 'of kindness' -- the coals-provoking-shame reading is one common interpretation among a few, and is better placed in commentary than baked into the verse itself.

verses.text: Like snow in summer or rain at harvest, honor does not fit a fool.
Like a sparrow that flutters or a swallow that flies, an undeserved curse does not come to rest.
A whip for the horse, a bridle for the donkey, and a rod for the back of fools.
Do not answer a fool according to that fool's foolishness, or you will become like the fool yourself.
Answer a fool according to that fool's foolishness, or the fool will think that fool is wise.
Sending a message by the hand of a fool is like cutting off your own feet or drinking poison.
Like the legs of someone who cannot walk hanging useless is a proverb in the mouth of a fool.
Giving honor to a fool is like tying a stone into a sling.
Like a thorn stuck in a drunkard's hand is a proverb in the mouth of a fool.
Like an archer who wounds everyone at random is whoever hires a fool or hires any passerby.
Like a dog that returns to its vomit is a fool who repeats the same foolishness.
Do you see someone who is wise in their own eyes? There is more hope for a fool than for that person.
A lazy person says: There is a lion in the road! A lion is loose in the streets!
As a door turns on its hinges, so a lazy person turns over in bed.
A lazy person buries a hand in the dish, and is too tired to bring it back to the mouth.
A lazy person thinks that person is wiser than seven people who can answer with good sense.
Whoever grabs a stray dog by the ears is like someone passing by who meddles in a quarrel that is not their own.
Like a madman who shoots burning arrows that can kill,
So is the person who tricks a neighbor and says: I was only joking!
Without wood a fire goes out; without gossip an argument stops.
As charcoal keeps embers glowing and wood feeds a fire, so a quarrelsome person keeps conflict going.
The words of a gossip are like delicious food; they go down to the innermost parts of the body.
Burning lips and a wicked heart are like a glaze covering a piece of cheap clay pottery.
A hateful person disguises that person's feelings with lying lips, while storing up deceit within.
When that hateful person speaks kindly, do not believe it, because there are seven detestable things in that person's heart.
That hateful person's hatred may be concealed by deception, but that deceitful person's wickedness will be exposed in public.
Whoever digs a pit will fall into it, and whoever rolls a stone will have that stone roll back on them.
A lying tongue hates the people it hurts, and a flattering mouth causes ruin.

26.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Hebrew text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy, with every pronoun's referent named explicitly (Deaf-first clarity standard) and each verse capitalized. V10 is one of the most textually disputed verses in Proverbs (the Hebrew word rab can mean 'great' or, in context, imply an archer); used the modern reading favored by most scholars given the surrounding context about fools, rather than the KJV's italicized interpretive insertion 'the great God' (the KJV translators themselves marked 'God' and 'things' as supplied words, not in the original text). V18's 'firebrands' updated to 'burning arrows' to remove a 17th-century term while avoiding redundancy with 'arrows.' V22 corrected to match the v18:8 fix elsewhere in this book (KJV's 'wounds' -> 'delicious food').

verses.text: Do not boast about tomorrow, because you do not know what a day may bring.
Let someone else praise you, and not your own mouth; a stranger, and not your own lips.
A stone is heavy, and sand is a burden, but the anger of a fool is heavier than both.
Fury is cruel, and anger is a flood, but who can stand before jealousy?
Open correction is better than hidden love.
Wounds from a friend can be trusted, but an enemy multiplies kisses.
A satisfied person refuses even honey, but to a hungry person even something bitter tastes sweet.
Like a bird that strays from its nest is a person who strays from home.
Perfume and incense bring joy to the heart, and the sweetness of a friend comes from that friend's heartfelt advice.
Do not forsake your own friend or your father's friend, and do not go to your brother's house when trouble strikes; better a neighbor nearby than a brother far away.
My son, be wise, and make my heart glad, so that I can answer anyone who insults me.
A sensible person sees danger and hides, but the simple keep going and suffer for it.
Take the coat of a person who guarantees a loan for a stranger; hold that coat as security if that person does it for a stranger's benefit.
Whoever blesses a neighbor loudly early in the morning will be seen as cursing that neighbor instead.
A constant dripping on a rainy day and a quarrelsome wife are alike.
Restraining her is like restraining the wind, or grasping oil with your hand.
Iron sharpens iron, and one person sharpens another.
Whoever tends a fig tree will eat its fruit, and whoever cares for a master will be honored.
As water reflects a person's face, so a person's heart reveals who that person really is.
Hell and destruction are never full, and neither are human eyes.
The furnace tests silver, and the fire tests gold, but a person is tested by the praise that person receives.
Even if you crush a fool in a mortar, grinding that fool like grain with a pestle, that fool's foolishness will not leave.
Know well the condition of your flocks, and pay close attention to your herds,
Because riches do not last forever, and a crown is not secure for every generation.
When the hay is cut and new growth appears, and the mountain grasses are gathered in,
The lambs will provide your clothing, and the goats will bring the price of a field.
You will have plenty of goat's milk for food — for you, for your household, and to nourish your servant girls.

27.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Hebrew text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy, with every pronoun's referent named explicitly (Deaf-first clarity standard) and each verse capitalized. V20's 'hell' corrected to 'the grave' (Hebrew sheol), consistent with the rest of the book. V13 and v19 refined to remove remaining pronoun loops and clarify the mirror comparison.

verses.text: The wicked run away even when no one is chasing them, but the righteous are as bold as a lion.
When a land rebels, it has many rulers, but a leader with understanding and knowledge gives it lasting stability.
A poor person who oppresses the poor is like a driving rain that leaves no food.
Whoever abandons the law praises the wicked, but whoever keeps the law fights against the wicked.
Evil people do not understand justice, but those who seek the LORD understand everything.
Better a poor person who lives with integrity than a rich person whose ways are dishonest.
Whoever keeps the law is a wise child, but a companion of wild living disgraces that child's father.
Whoever grows wealthy through excessive interest and unjust gain is only storing it up for someone who will be kind to the poor.
Whoever refuses to listen to God's law — even that person's prayers are disgusting to the LORD.
Whoever leads honest people down an evil path will fall into that same trap, but people of integrity will inherit good things.
A rich person may think that rich person is wise, but a poor person with understanding sees right through that rich person's pride.
When the righteous succeed, there is great celebration, but when the wicked rise to power, people go into hiding.
Whoever conceals their sins will not prosper, but whoever confesses and stops doing those sins will find mercy.
Blessed is the person who always stays reverent, but whoever hardens their heart falls into trouble.
Like a roaring lion or a charging bear is a wicked ruler over poor people.
A ruler with no understanding oppresses people cruelly, but whoever hates unjust gain will enjoy a long life.
Whoever is guilty of murder will be a fugitive until death; let no one help that person.
Whoever walks with integrity will be kept safe, but whoever's ways are dishonest will suddenly fall.
Whoever works the land will have plenty of food, but whoever chases worthless ideas will have plenty of poverty.
A faithful person will be richly blessed, but whoever rushes to get rich will not go unpunished.
Showing favoritism is not good, yet some will do wrong for a mere piece of bread.
A greedy person is eager to get rich and does not realize that poverty is coming.
Whoever corrects someone will later earn more favor than whoever flatters with the tongue.
Whoever steals from their father or mother and says: It's not wrong — that person is a partner to a criminal.
A greedy person stirs up conflict, but whoever trusts in the LORD will prosper.
Whoever trusts in their own mind is a fool, but whoever walks in wisdom will be kept safe.
Whoever gives to the poor will not be in need, but a person who shuts his eyes to poor people will receive many curses.
When the wicked rise to power, people hide, but when the wicked perish, the righteous flourish.

28.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Hebrew text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy, with every pronoun's referent named explicitly (Deaf-first clarity standard) and each verse capitalized. V9's 'turns a deaf ear' rewritten to 'refuses to listen' -- this site never uses 'deaf' as a negative metaphor for disobedience, given the audience. V11, v13, v19, and v27 refined for sharper explicit-noun clarity and to match wording used elsewhere in the book.

verses.text: Whoever is often corrected but remains stubborn will suddenly be destroyed beyond healing.
When the righteous are in charge, the people celebrate, but when the wicked rule, the people groan.
Whoever loves wisdom brings joy to that person's father, but whoever spends time with prostitutes wastes that person's wealth.
A king brings stability to the land through justice, but a king who demands bribes tears it down.
Whoever flatters a neighbor is spreading a net for that neighbor's feet.
An evil person is trapped by that person's own sin, but the righteous sing and rejoice.
The righteous care about justice for the poor, but the wicked have no such concern.
Mockers can throw a whole city into turmoil, but wise people turn away anger.
If a wise person takes a fool to court, the fool only rages or laughs, and there is no peace.
Bloodthirsty people hate an honest person, but the upright seek to protect that honest person's life.
A fool blurts out all that fool's anger, but a wise person holds it back and stays calm.
If a ruler listens to lies, that ruler's officials all become wicked.
The poor person and the oppressor have this in common: the LORD gives light to both their eyes.
If a king judges the poor fairly, that king's throne will be secure forever.
The rod and correction bring wisdom, but a child left without guidance disgraces that child's mother.
When the wicked increase, sin increases too, but the righteous will see the wicked fall.
Correct your child, and your child will bring you peace; your child will bring delight to your soul.
Where people ignore God's word, people run wild, but blessed is whoever keeps the law.
A servant cannot be corrected by words alone; even if that servant understands, that servant will not respond.
Do you see someone who speaks too quickly? There is more hope for a fool than for that person.
A master who pampers a servant from childhood will find that servant rebellious and unruly in the end!
An angry person stirs up conflict, and a hot-tempered person commits many sins.
A person's pride will bring that person down, but a humble spirit gains honor.
Whoever partners with a thief is an enemy to their own life; a thief's partner hears the warning in court but stays silent.
Fearing what people think is a trap, but whoever trusts in the LORD is kept safe.
Many seek the favor of a ruler, but justice for everyone comes from the LORD.
The righteous detest a dishonest person, and the wicked detest whoever lives with integrity.

29.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Hebrew text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy, with every pronoun's referent named explicitly (Deaf-first clarity standard) and each verse capitalized. V18 clarifies 'vision' (Hebrew khazon, divine revelation) rather than physical eyesight. V21's genuinely uncertain Hebrew word (manon, occurring only this once in the Bible) rewritten for clear cause-and-effect: pampering leads to a rebellious, unruly servant. V24 clarifies the legal-witness scene; v25 translates the Hebrew kherdat adam ('dread of man') as 'fearing what people think.'

verses.text: These are the words of Agur, son of Jakeh — an oracle. This man declared to Ithiel, to Ithiel and Ucal:
Surely I am more foolish than anyone else; I do not have a human's understanding.
I have not learned wisdom, and I do not have knowledge of the Holy One.

Who has gone up to heaven and come down? Who has gathered up the wind in cupped hands? Who has wrapped up the waters in a cloak? Who has set in place all the ends of the earth? What is that person's name, and what is that person's son's name — tell me if you know!
Every word of God is flawless; God is a shield to those who take refuge in God.
Do not add to God's words, or God will correct you and prove you a liar.
Two things I ask of you, LORD; do not refuse me before I die:
Keep falsehood and lies far from me; give me neither poverty nor riches, but give me only the food I need.
Otherwise, I may have too much and deny you and say: Who is the LORD? Or I may become poor and steal, and dishonor the name of my God.
Do not slander a servant to that servant's master, or the servant will curse you, and you will be found guilty.
There is a generation that curses their father and does not bless their mother.
There is a generation that is pure in their own eyes, yet is not washed from their filth.
There is a generation whose eyes are ever so proud, whose glances are so arrogant.
There is a generation whose teeth are swords, whose jaws are knives, to devour the poor from the earth and the needy from among people.
The leech has two daughters, and they always cry: Give! Give! There are three things that are never satisfied, four that never say: Enough!
The grave, the childless womb, land that never gets enough water, and fire that never says: Enough!
The eye that mocks a father, and refuses to obey a mother, will be picked out by ravens in the valley and eaten by young vultures.
There are three things too amazing for me, four that I do not understand:
The way of an eagle in the sky, the way of a snake on a rock, the way of a ship in the middle of the sea, and the way of a man with a young woman.
This is the way of a woman who commits adultery: she eats, wipes her mouth, and says: I have done nothing wrong.
Under three things the earth trembles, under four it cannot stand:
A servant who becomes king, a fool who is stuffed with food,
An unloved woman who gets married, and a servant girl who takes her mistress's place.
Four things on earth are small, but they are extremely wise:
Ants are not strong, yet they store up their food in summer;
Hyraxes are creatures with little power, yet they make their homes in the rocks;
Locusts have no king, yet they all advance together in ranks;
A lizard can be caught with the hands, yet it lives inside kings' palaces.
There are three things that walk with fine bearing, four that move with grace:
A lion, mightiest among beasts, who backs down from nothing,
A strutting rooster, a male goat, and a king whom no one dares to challenge.
If you have been foolish and exalted yourself, or if you have plotted evil, stop talking and put your hand over your mouth!
As churning milk produces butter, and twisting a nose produces blood, so stirring up anger produces conflict.

30.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Hebrew text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy, with every pronoun's referent named explicitly (Deaf-first clarity standard) and each verse capitalized. V16's 'the grave' matches sheol as used throughout this book. V26's 'conies' updated to 'hyraxes,' the actual animal (a small rock-dwelling mammal, not a rabbit as 'coney' suggests to modern readers). V31's debated 'greyhound' rendered as 'strutting rooster,' the reading favored by most modern translations for this obscure Hebrew phrase.

verses.text: Better to be poor and honest than to be a liar and a fool.
It is not good for a person to be without knowledge. If you hurry and do something too quickly, you will make mistakes.
People destroy their lives when they do foolish things, then they get angry and blame the LORD and say it is the LORD's fault.
When a person is rich, that person has many friends, but when that person becomes poor, that person has no friends.
A false witness will be punished, and someone who tells lies will not escape.
Everyone wants to be friends with an important person. They also want to be friends with someone who gives away gifts.

A poor man's brothers do not like that poor man, and that poor man's friends will avoid that poor man even more. When that poor man really needs them, they stay away. There is no one there to help that poor man.
Whoever gains wisdom loves that person's own life; whoever keeps understanding will find success.
A false witness will be punished, and someone who tells lies will perish.
It is not normal for a fool to be rich or for a slave to rule over princes!
A wise man does not become angry quickly; that wise man always wants to forgive the mistakes of other people.
The shouts of an angry king are like a roaring lion, but the king's kind words are like the dew on the grass.
A foolish child brings a lot of trouble to that child's father and a complaining wife is like water dripping non-stop from a roof.
People receive houses and money from their parents, but a good wise wife is a gift from the LORD.
A lazy person sleeps all day, and an idle worker goes hungry.
People who obey the commandments of the LORD will live, but whoever ignores God's ways will die.
Whoever is kind to the poor lends to the LORD, and the LORD will reward that person for what that person has done.
Correct your child while there is still hope, and do not let that child's crying stop you.
A person who gets angry quickly will always have trouble. If you help that person, you will have to help that person again and again.
If you listen to what people teach you and you learn from them, you will have wisdom in the end.
People make a lot of plans about what they want to do, but the advice of the LORD will endure.
What people desire most is loyalty; better to be a poor person than a liar.
Respecting the LORD gives you a good life, one that is satisfying and protected during trouble.
A lazy man puts that man's hand in a dish to get food, but that man is too lazy to bring the food back to his mouth.
If you punish a mocker, the simpleminded will learn a lesson; if you correct the wise, the wise will be all the wiser.
A child who steals from that child's father and chases away that child's mother causes shame and brings disappointment.
My son, if you stop learning, you will turn your back on knowledge.
Using a criminal as a witness makes a joke of justice. Sinful people love to do things that are wrong.
Judgments are prepared for mockers, and a whip for the back of fools.

verses.text: Wine is deceiving, and alcohol causes fighting; everyone led astray by them lacks wisdom.
People should be afraid of an angry king, like they are of a lion that roars. If you make the king angry, you can lose your life.
It is an honor for people to stop from strife: Any fool can start an argument.
Because of the cold a lazy person will not prepare their fields: then in the summer they shall beg for food, and no one shall give to them.
Getting information from someone can be like getting water from a deep well. If you are wise, you can draw it out.
There are many people who say: You can trust me. But there are only a few of them that do what they promise.
Good people live in the right way and are honest. God blesses their children who live like they do.
When a king sits on a throne to judge people, that king can see through evil with sharp eyes.
No one can say, I have made my heart clean, have never done anything sinful.
The LORD hates people that use the wrong weights and measures to cheat others.
Even children show what they are like by the things they do. You can see if their actions are pure and right.
The Lord has given some people ears to hear and some people eyes to see.
Do not love excessive sleep, or you will become poor; Open your eyes so that you can do your work and you will be satisfied with bread.
When a person is buying something, they always say: It's no good. It costs too much. Then they go away and tell others what a good deal they got.
There is gold, and an abundance of jewels; But the words of someone who is wise are even more precious.
Take the garment of anyone who puts up collateral for a stranger; hold it in pledge if that person does it for an unfamiliar woman.
If you have cheated someone to get food, it will taste good in the beginning but in the end, The guilt and consequence will be bitter.
Get good advice before you make your plans. Before you start a war, ask for the advice of wise advisors.
A gossip goes around telling secrets. Don't be friends with someone who does not care what that person says.
Those who would curse their father or mother are like a lamp that goes out in the darkest night.
If a person gets an inheritance too quickly, while that person is still young, it will not be a blessing in the end.
Don't say: I will get even for this wrong. Wait for the LORD to handle the matter.
The Lord hates people who cheat when they weigh things and who are dishonest
No person knows what will happen to that person. It is the Lord who decides what will happen to us.
Think carefully before you promise to give something to God. Later, you might wish you had not made that promise.
A king who is wise can find out who is guilty and punish those who have done wrong.
The LORD gave us our mind and conscience; we cannot hide our thoughts and doings from Him.
Mercy and truth protect a king, and his throne is made secure by mercy.
We admire a young man for his strength, but we respect an old man for his gray hair.
Sometimes it takes a painful experience to make us change our ways.

verses.text: These are the wise sayings that King Lemuel’s mother taught him:
My child, I am your mother. I prayed to God and He gave you to me.
Don't waste your strength or your life on women. Do not give your efforts to things that destroy kings.
Lemuel, kings should not drink wine, Or for rulers to desire strong drink.
If kings drink too much, kings forget the law and fail to protect the rights of poor people.
Alcohol is for the dying, and wine for those of bitter of heart
Let them drink and forget their troubles. Let them forget about all their suffering.
Speak up for people who cannot speak for themselves. Help people who are in trouble.
Speak for them and be fair when you judge, and protect the people who can not help themselves and who have nothing.
A capable, noble wife is hard to find. She is worth far more than rubies.
Her husband trusts her completely, so her husband will never need to steal to get by.
She does good for her husband all her life, and she never brings her husband trouble.
She gets wool and flax and enjoys making things with her hands.
She is like the merchants' ships; she brings her food from far away.
She gets up while it is dark and she prepares food for her family and for the servants who work for her.
She looks carefully at a field and buys it and she plants the vineyard
Her arms are strong, and she keeps on working.
When she sees people wanting to buy the things that she makes, she works all night.
She makes thread with her hands, and she weaves at the loom and makes clothes.
She loves giving to poor people and those who can not protect themselves and who have nothing.
She does not worry about her family when it snows because they all have scarlet wool clothes.
She makes blankets and her clothes are made of linen and purple wool.
Everyone knows her husband. Her husband sits with the leaders of the land at the gate.
She makes clothes and sells them, and she gives the merchants sashes to sell.
Strength and dignity are her clothing, and she laughs at the future without fear.
She always speaks words of wisdom, and she teaches her people to be friendly.
She oversees the care of her house. She is never lazy.
Her children respect and praise her, and her husband says she is a good wife. Her husband says:
There are a lot of good women, but you are better than all of them.
A woman does not always stay young and beautiful, but you should always praise a woman who serves and fears the Lord.
She must get the reward for her hard work, and everyone in the city must praise her.

V5 clarifies 'they' as 'kings'; v10 restores the Hebrew khayil (strength/capability/valor) rather than a vaguer 'honest character'; v21 restores 'scarlet wool' (Hebrew shanim); v25 restores the vivid 'strength and dignity as clothing' metaphor.
